reproduce.module: Always On Top border and Windows taskbar
reproduce.expected_result: No orphan outline overlays another app during Peek; the pinned target stays pinned and its border returns correctly afterward.
steps: Hover another taskbar thumbnail then enter its Peek preview; record target/border visibility, DWM attributes and z-order.
Leave the thumbnail and verify the original border is restored without repinning or stealing focus.
Compare previewing the pinned window itself, another app, minimize/restore and virtual-desktop transitions.
Check relevant Windows shell versions with Peek enabled and disabled.
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable and current development build
prerequisites: Pin a disposable normal window with a visible border; keep another application foreground.

actions.label: Trace pinned border through taskbar Peek

judgment.recommended_action: Trace Peek enter/leave for tracked and border windows, then restore border visibility without changing the pin state.
judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied the trigger and visual proof. A maintainer can trace the target and border HWND visibility through Peek and choose the narrow visibility policy; removing topmost or repeatedly recreating unrelated windows is not justified.
evidence: Read the complete0.64.1 report, empty comments and timeline and inspected both supplied images.
The first screenshot shows the pinned Calculator border; the second shows that border remaining over another app while a taskbar thumbnail is hovered.
Current WindowBorder initialization marks the separate border window DWMWA_EXCLUDED_FROM_PEEK and positions it behind its tracked window.
Current timer refreshes border position/properties; foreground RefreshBorders handles current virtual desktop ownership, not an explicit Peek lifecycle.
No current taskbar Peek session was executed; the attribute and screenshot are a concrete investigation lead, not proof that simply removing the attribute is safe.

proposed_fixes.title: Track the pinned border visibility across taskbar Peek
plan: Measure target/border HWND state through Peek before choosing between DWM policy and explicit visibility handling.
Apply the narrow visibility correction without altering target topmost state or activation.
Restore normal border behavior on Peek exit, minimize/restore and desktop switches.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the separate border window remains visible when its tracked window is suppressed by Peek; current code explicitly excludes the border from Peek.

confidence.rationale: Screenshots and exact current DWM/refresh source support the lead; no current shell trace or safe correction was executed.

verification: Exercise other-app and pinned-app thumbnail previews.
Verify no orphan or permanently hidden borders, focus theft or lost pin state.

title: The top window still displays the window border when move the mouse to the preview window over the app icon on the taskbar，
